brief: Goldman Sachs's daily market wrap, structured as independent sections rather than one argument. Lead item: a weaker-than-expected September payrolls print (29k vs 90k consensus) cut market-implied odds of an October Fed hike below 20%, a move GS itself expects not to happen; the S&P 500 rose 73bps to a record even as the 10-year held at 5.27% and mortgages topped 7.3%. Hedge fund long/short net leverage fell to a near-5-year low while Europe saw its largest net buying in five years, and the median stock sits 17% off its high despite the index being only 2% away. The Pentagon is sending a third carrier group and 10k troops to the Gulf as Tehran readies a response, keeping Brent volatile near $102. Q3 earnings season starts next week on 27% consensus EPS growth, over half tied to AI infrastructure spending and concentrated in the top 10 stocks (68% of growth, Micron and Nvidia alone 34%). Separate items: Amazon and four European names added to Conviction Lists, a memory-pricing recovery, and gold-discovery scarcity despite record prices.
